chunks: It was narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
I was shown Hell, and I saw Amr ibn Luhayy, a short, red-skinned, blue-eyed man, dragging a baton in Hell. I asked: Who is this? It was told: He is Amr ibn Luhayy.

key_terms.أَحْمَرَ أَزْرَقَ: Red and blue (referring to skin/eye color or complexion)
key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ لُحَيٍّ: Amr ibn Luhayy, a prominent pre-Islamic Arab leader

ai.seo_question: Who is Amr ibn Luhayy and what did the Prophet see of him in Hell during the Mi'raj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Amr ibn Luhayy as the pivotal figure who introduced *Jahiliyyah* idolatry to the Quraysh, a status that earned him a unique place in Hell even during the Prophet’s Mi'raj. The specific description of him dragging a 'baton' (qasabah) symbolizes his role as the shepherd of idols who led the Arabs astray, serving as a foundational historical context for the spiritual darkness addressed in Shia eschatology.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 88 - It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s) that he said:
I was shown Hell during my journey of Meraj. I saw a short stature man, Amr bin Lahih paying with his baton in Hell. I asked: Who is this? I was told: He is Amr bin Lahih.
